answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring agents to tend a personal garden of reciprocal attestations: each must continually exchange and renew a verification signal with a diverse set of peers. At the zenith, an attacker faces multiplicative costs because fabricating one fake identity demands forging an entire dense subgraph of living mutual signals that peers will reject if inconsistent, making large-scale identity farming prohibitively expensive in both compute and coordination time.
